title: Bridal hair and hijab bridal styling: from the trial to the wedding day
seoTitle: Bridal Hair and Hijab Bridal Styling Guide | Emrahair
description: Bridal hair and hijab bridal styling guide: updos, half-up styles, crowns, when to book a trial and how to prepare. Read it before you choose a style.
lede: Choosing bridal hair means thinking about the dress, the veil or crown, your hair itself and how long the day will be; hijab bridal styling adds volume and a secure base under the scarf. This guide walks you through it step by step, from updo or half-up to the trial and the wedding morning.

sections.heading: How do you choose a bridal hairstyle?
body: Good bridal hair and the dress read as one look. With a high or closed neckline, wearing the hair up shows off the neck and the collar. With an open back or a strapless gown, a low updo or loose waves soften the line of the back. If the dress has heavy embellishment, the hair is usually kept simpler.

The veil and crown shape the decision too. A veil is usually pinned above or below the updo, so where the updo sits depends on how the veil should fall. A crown sits best on a base with some volume at the top, and a heavy crown needs a firmer foundation. The length and density of your hair then decide which style will hold all day.

sections.heading: Updo, half-up or loose waves?
body: The updo (topuz) is the most requested bridal style, and it comes in very different versions. A sleek, smooth updo looks classic and formal. A messy updo is softer and more romantic for a wedding: a few face-framing pieces and a loosely textured bun are especially popular at outdoor weddings.

A half-up style gathers the top section and leaves the rest in waves. It is a good middle ground for brides who want both structure and movement, and for anyone looking for an evening-gown look. Fully loose waves are the most natural option, but they need careful preparation to hold their shape through a long, humid day. Engagement hair is usually simpler and worn down, while braids or a polished ponytail are comfortable for a henna night or a long party.
list: Sleek classic updo: formal, and easy to pair with a veil and crown.
Messy updo: romantic and natural, soft in photos.
Half-up: the structure of an updo with the movement of loose hair.
Loose waves: the most natural look, and the most careful preparation.

sections.heading: How is hijab bridal hair prepared?
body: In hijab bridal styling the hair is not seen, but what sits underneath shapes the whole look. The goal is balanced volume under the scarf and a firm base that will not slip during the day. That volume usually comes from a bun at the nape or the crown, sometimes with a light volume insert. Where the bun sits depends on the silhouette you want and whether you will wear a crown.

The bonnet (bone) goes over the bun and is secured with pins, and the scarf, plus a veil if you wear one, is arranged over it. Crowns, brooches and pins go on last, with their weight spread so it does not rest on one spot. The fabric matters as well: slippery fabrics need more securing. Over a long day, pins that do not press are as important as the look itself.

If you are planning a hijab bridal style, it is best to talk with the salon before booking about what can be done and how the preparation should be planned. Bringing your own scarf, bonnet and accessories to a trial shows the result far more clearly.

sections.heading: When should you do a bridal hair trial?
body: A trial is the easiest way to avoid surprises on the day. Many brides book their trial a few weeks before the wedding, which leaves time to adjust the style and to finish color or treatment plans. Simply ask when booking whether a trial is possible and how it is arranged.

During the trial, photograph the style from several angles and look at the photos in daylight too. Notice how it looks with the veil or crown on and how it holds a few hours later. When planning the wedding-day schedule, keep in mind that bridal hair usually takes 1 to 2 hours depending on the style, and add the time for makeup. Special dates fill up quickly, so booking as soon as your date is set makes things easier.

sections.heading: Preparing your hair in the weeks before
body: If you are planning color or balayage, doing it a few weeks before the wedding gives the tone time to settle and leaves room for a correction if needed. A trim one or two weeks ahead also gives the hair time to settle into its new shape.

It is safer not to leave services such as [keratin treatment](/keratin) to the final week. Because keratin leaves hair smoother and silkier, it can affect how well an updo or waves hold, so talk about the timing based on the style you have chosen. Skipping heavy, oily treatments the day before helps the hair hold the style better.

Hands are part of the photos too. A manicure and gel polish a day or two before the wedding keep nails at their freshest. At Emrahair, [manicures and pedicures](/manikur-pedikur) are done by Gizem Değişener; a manicure is [[33-1]] and gel polish on the hands is [[67-1]].

sections.heading: What to bring on the wedding day
body: Having everything in one bag on the wedding morning means the time goes to your hair, not to searching:
list: Photos of the styles you like and of your trial
A photo of your dress, especially the neckline and back
Your veil, crown, clips and other hair accessories
For hijab bridal styling: your scarf, bonnet and pins
A button-front or zip-front top, so nothing has to go over your head once your hair is done
A few spare pins for touch-ups during the day

faq.q: How long does bridal hair take?
faq.a: Depending on the style, bridal hair usually takes 1 to 2 hours. A veil, a crown or hijab preparation can add to that. When you plan the wedding-day schedule, plan hair and makeup time together.

faq.q: How do you create volume under a hijab for a wedding?
faq.a: Volume usually comes from a bun at the nape or the crown under the scarf, sometimes with a light volume insert. The bonnet is pinned over the bun, and the scarf and accessories go on last. Trying it with your own scarf makes the result clear.

faq.q: When should I book a bridal hair trial?
faq.a: A trial is usually done a few weeks before the wedding. That leaves time to adjust the style and finish any color or treatment plans. Bring a photo of your dress and your accessories to the trial.

faq.q: Is a messy updo a good choice for a wedding?
faq.a: Yes, the messy updo is one of the most loved wedding styles and gives a romantic, natural look. To keep it from falling apart, the base is built firmly and the face-framing pieces are left in a controlled way. At Emrahair, an updo is listed at [[25-1]].
